bullets: Racing is fundamentally about risk management rather than nerve — the crash that ends a season is almost never the scary-looking one but the boring risk that wasn't named.
Naming a risk before it names you removes half the danger — the risk you can describe is the one you can design around.
A race run must be ridden as a system rather than a list of corners — mistakes come from how one section sets up the next.
A full season of logged crashes revealed that causes were always two turns upstream from the actual crash point.
Race lines and financial portfolios are both systems of correlated bets — the same discipline of managing interactions applies to both.
